text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.7% today to $139.55, continuing a pullback from its peak of $142.28 four days ago. The decline came as crude oil prices slipped—US oil dropped to $89.62 per barrel, down from recent highs—and despite geopolitical tensions that briefly supported energy prices. Iran's escalation of threats against U.S. forces in the Middle East and the arrival of a third American carrier in the Gulf had the potential to tighten oil supply and push prices higher, but that support wasn't enough to overcome the broader momentum shift.

The two-week drop of 3.4% reflects a more cautious energy market even as heating oil prices remain elevated (up 59% year-over-year) and winter demand typically supports refined products. The slight weakness in crude prices suggests investors may be pricing in weaker demand growth or concerns about global economic slowdown, despite tight supply conditions that geopolitical risks typically underscore.
